title: Claude built this rigged robot in Blender from one concept image, 26 stages, every step recorded
author: droid_man_
selftext:
I've spent the last few weeks on a setup that turns a single concept image into a 3D model in Blender. Claude (Opus) does the modeling through the Blender MCP, and OBS records every stage. This is the first full run: the mascot of my channel.

How it works:

* **Reference:** one AI concept image, plus orthographic and detail sheets on a fixed grid. A separate agent audits them for contradictions, and the proportions are measured from the sheets into a spec.
* **Build:** 26 logged stages: blockout, head, body, arms and legs, materials, emissive face, rig, wave and walk animation, lighting, final render.
* **Fixes:** I reviewed the result and asked for 3 fix passes (thighs and knees, feet and ankles, how the leg joints sit). Claude made those too, and they are in the video as their own stages.
* **Result:** 25 parts, an armature with leg IK and knee poles (every part rides one bone), a wave and a walk cycle, rendered in EEVEE. Around 19 minutes of recorded Blender work. The recorder pauses whenever Claude isn't working in Blender.

Being honest about the limits:

* I haven't checked the topology or the vertex count yet. The next video shows the mesh as a check, and I'll try to bring the vertex count down. I wouldn't call it game-ready until then.
* It's hard-surface with rigid parts on bones, not a skinned organic character.
* The fix passes came from my own review. It didn't get everything right on the first try.

I'm planning to put the whole setup on GitHub, with a README on how it works, what it can do and where it breaks. Would you use something like this in your pipeline? What would you need from it? Any feedback is welcome.

comments.author: droid_man_
comments.body:
Full video (2:53): [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0fm9sb5-xU](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0fm9sb5-xU)  
Made with Blender 5.1, Claude Opus and the Blender MCP. Happy to answer questions about the setup.

comments.author: xWranglerWranglerx
comments.body: are you feeding obs recordings to claude or something?

replies.author: droid_man_
replies.body: Nope, it's the other way around. Claude controls Blender directly through Blender's MCP add-on and checks its work with viewport screenshots. It also controls the recording: it starts OBS itself, and the recording pauses whenever it isn't actively working in Blender. Afterwards I speed the footage up into a timelapse. Claude never sees the recording.

replies.author: _KoingWolf_
replies.body: Thanks for sharing this, I try to tell people about how poweful MCP is with prompting and screenshot rules, and they dismiss it and seem to assume im talking about direct control.

replies.author: droid_man_
replies.body:
Yeah, I recently watched a video that tested three different approaches to using Claude with Blender:

1. Headless Claude + Blender
2. Claude + Blender MCP
3. Claude controlling your computer to interact with Blender

The third option was dropped after the first test because it took way too long and the results were terrible.

The first two approaches are both really good, but each has its own pros and cons.

Here's the video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TlYFme-3RCI&t=91s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TlYFme-3RCI&t=91s)

comments.author: droid_man_
comments.body:
So, the end results were pretty much the same. The main difference was when you wanted to create multiple things at once.

With the headless approach, you would have multiple Blender instances running in the background, which was quite resource-intensive. With MCP, everything could be done in the same Blender window, with each agent focusing only on its own work.

That was the main conclusion of the video.

replies.author: deReaLizedGames
replies.body: Oh that's actually super helpful,  I was running into this exact issue this weekend when trying to build multiple characters at once lol.  It could only do 3 at a time. headless Thanks for the info!!
